You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**From:** AI legal assistant (buyer side)
**Status:** Privileged working draft – for internal review. Seller material treated as adverse-party drafting, not as agreed or verified facts.

---

## 1. Headline assessment

The Seller's "fair and balanced package" departs from our playbook on almost every point and, in several places, goes further than a normal seller-friendly opening position: it collapses the Fundamental/Title regime into the general regime, removes the fraud carve-out by implication, builds in a double knowledge bar (buyer actual knowledge *plus* "discoverable from the data room or public records"), and treats Bluefen consent and Riverlark release as satisfied by a reasonable-endeavours covenant and a post-Completion release respectively.

Notably, the Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts the Seller Update on the two most important pre-Completion items: it admits that **no final Bluefen consent** and **no Riverlark discharge** are in the data room. That is useful – we should hold them to their own disclosure.

No item in the Seller package is acceptable as drafted. One item (the 20% cap / 18-month period) is within our conditional fallback range but **cannot be conceded** because no written authority from Amelia Frost exists for this draft.

---

## 2. Issue-by-issue comparison

### 2.1 General Warranty cap – Clause 12.1
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Cap | 20% / AUD 4,800,000 | 25% / AUD 6,000,000 (opening); 20% only with Amelia Frost written authority identifying the draft |

**Analysis.** The Seller has pitched straight at our fallback. We have no authority to accept it for this draft. Conceding now would also surrender it without trading it against anything (e.g. 24-month period, first-dollar basket).

**Position.** Counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not signal that 20% is available. If the principal later authorises 20%, it should be traded for the thresholds/time-limit points, not given free.

### 2.2 Thresholds – Clause 12.2
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 |
| Basket | AUD 250,000 | AUD 50,000 |
| Recovery | Excess over basket only ("deductible") | First dollar once exceeded ("tipping") |

**Analysis.** Three separate departures. The de minimis is 5× ours, the basket 5× ours, and the deductible structure permanently removes AUD 250,000 of recovery. On a AUD 24m deal the Seller's package would leave a large band of mid-sized claims (data/IP remediation, employee-related liabilities, contract disputes) effectively uninsured.

**Position.** Revert to AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / tipping basket. The deductible-versus-tipping point is the most valuable of the three and should be held hardest.

### 2.3 Time limits and "all Claims" override – Clause 12.3 / 13
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| General claims | 18 months | 24 months (18 only with Amelia Frost written approval – none given) |
| Scope | "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" | Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override |

**Analysis.** 18 months is again our fallback, unauthorised. The more dangerous element is the second sentence: a default rule that every limitation applies to every Claim unless an express carve-out exists. Combined with 12.8/20.5 (below) and the Seller's Fundamental/Title proposal, this reverses the burden – any specific indemnity, covenant claim, Tax claim or Title claim we fail to expressly carve out is silently subjected to the 18-month period, the AUD 4.8m cap and the AUD 250k deductible basket. That is the "hidden general-regime override" our playbook prohibits.

**Position.** 24 months for general Warranties. Delete the "all Claims" default. Replace with an express scope clause: the limitations in Clause 12 apply **only** to general Warranty Claims and not to Fundamental/Title Warranties, Tax Warranties and Tax indemnity, IP Warranties (pending agreed regime), specific indemnities (including Ironquay), payment obligations, covenants, or any fraud-related claim.

### 2.4 Fundamental / Title Warranties
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Regime | Same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity" | Separate regime: 100% cap, ≥ 6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar |

**Analysis.** This is not administrative simplification; it caps our recovery for a defective-title or no-authority claim at 20% of price and extinguishes it after 18 months. If Harbourglass does not own or cannot validly transfer the shares, we would be AUD 24m out with a AUD 4.8m claim. Market practice on an Australian private M&A deal of this size is a 100% cap and a long period (typically 6–7 years) for title/capacity. The Seller's rationale is not credible.

**Position.** Reject outright. Insert a separate Fundamental Warranty regime: 100% of purchase price cap, minimum six years, no de minimis, no basket, no buyer-knowledge qualifier, not subject to 9.3/12.8/20.5.

### 2.5 Fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct – Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Carve-out | None. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature" | Carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable; non-waivable |

**Analysis.** The Seller draft does not merely omit the carve-out; "all Claims of any nature" is drafted to capture fraud. Courts are reluctant to enforce exclusion of liability for a party's own fraud, but we should not rely on that – the clause will still be used to resist and delay, and the non-reliance language in 20.5 will be deployed to attack misleading-conduct claims. This is a non-negotiable point under our playbook and the deal team has no authority to soften it.

**Position.** Insert an express, overriding carve-out: nothing in the Agreement limits or excludes liability for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct of the Seller or any person for whom it is responsible, to the maximum extent permitted by law; such claims are outside Clauses 9.3, 12 and 20.5 and the time limits. Mark it as a no-concession item.

### 2.6 Disclosure – Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2, 1.4
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Standard | General disclosure of entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" | Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure |

**Analysis.** Paragraph 1.1 is a whole-data-room disclosure; 1.2 adds public registers. Together with Clause 8.3 this means every Warranty is qualified by anything that could be found anywhere in the data room or on ASIC, PPSR or IP Australia, whether or not it was flagged. Paragraph 1.4 (no admission that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is required) is an attempt to disclose the facts while denying their legal consequence – i.e. it asks us to accept the risk while the Seller denies it exists.

**Position.** Replace with a "fair disclosure" standard: a matter is disclosed only if disclosed in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Delete 1.1 and 1.2 general disclosure. Paragraph 1.4 may stay as a no-admission statement only if it is made clear it does not prevent any matter from constituting a breach or limit any indemnity.

### 2.7 Buyer knowledge – Clause 8.3
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Exclusion | No claim for any matter the Buyer or advisers "had knowledge" of, including anything "discoverable from the data room or public records" | Delete blanket exclusion; any qualifier must be limited to named Seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry; never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities |

**Analysis.** This is a constructive-knowledge bar: "discoverable" is a prudent-search standard, so the Buyer is deemed to know whatever a perfect reviewer could have found. It would nullify the Warranties on exactly the matters we diligence hardest. Attributing advisers' knowledge compounds it. It also has no exclusion for Fundamental Warranties or indemnities.

**Position.** Delete Clause 8.3. If the Seller insists on a knowledge concept anywhere, it belongs on the Seller side only: Seller Warranties qualified by "so far as the Seller is aware" are confined to the actual knowledge of named individuals (to be identified by Seller) after due and careful enquiry. No buyer-knowledge bar at all; expressly no application to Title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

### 2.8 Bluefen change-control consent – Clause 3 / 6.3
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Mechanism | Reasonable endeavours; consent "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" | Effective consent **and** evidence that conditions in cl. 11.3 are satisfied, before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours insufficient |

**Analysis.** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue. The Seller's own Disclosure Letter (para 2) confirms consent has **not** been obtained and no evidence of condition satisfaction is in the data room. The Seller Update nonetheless says the consent "is addressed". The condition-satisfaction wording is the trap: a written consent subject to unsatisfied cl. 11.3 conditions is not an effective consent, yet under the Seller draft it would deem the CP satisfied and Completion would proceed with the key customer entitled to walk.

**Position.** Condition Precedent: receipt of unconditional written consent from Bluefen under cl. 11.2, in form reasonably satisfactory to Buyer, together with evidence satisfactory to Buyer that all conditions under cl. 11.3 have been satisfied or waived by Bluefen. Seller obligation: all reasonable endeavours is insufficient – require "best endeavours" or at minimum an obligation to procure, with Buyer right of involvement in communications. Buyer may waive the CP; Seller may not. Consider a Bluefen-specific indemnity or price adjustment if consent is obtained on altered commercial terms.

### 2.9 Riverlark facility – Clause 2 / 7
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Mechanism | Release "to be provided following Completion" | Current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion; post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval |

**Analysis.** ~AUD 3.2m is outstanding. The deal is debt-free/cash-free, so this must come out of the price or be repaid from Completion funds – a post-Completion release means we acquire a company still encumbered (DD-003 cl. 8.1 change-of-control; cl. 9.2 discharge), with the Seller receiving the full price and then controlling the repayment. Disclosure Letter para 3 confirms neither repayment nor discharge has occurred. We also need to check whether the share sale itself triggers cl. 8.1 default absent lender consent.

**Position.** Require: (a) payout letter from Riverlark dated no earlier than 2 business days before Completion; (b) payout amount paid directly to Riverlark from Completion funds and deducted from the amount payable to the Seller; (c) executed releases of all security (including PPSR discharges and any guarantees) delivered at Completion, in escrow if necessary; (d) Riverlark's confirmation that cl. 8.1 is not triggered or is waived. A post-Completion release is not to be accepted without an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark and Amelia Frost's approval – neither exists.

### 2.10 Employee bonuses (DD-005) – funds flow
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Treatment | "A matter for the Seller", not itemised in funds flow | AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them |

**Analysis.** The bonuses are Completion-triggered, so the liability crystallises in the Company at the moment we own it. "A matter for the Seller" is not a funding mechanism – once Completion occurs, the Company (now ours) is the employer and will pay. On-costs (superannuation, payroll tax, possibly leave loading/workers comp) are not addressed by the Seller at all (Disclosure Letter para 5). The continued-employment conditions may reduce the figure but do not justify omitting it.

**Position.** Treat the bonuses and associated on-costs as Debt or a Transaction Expense in the price mechanics, deducted from the Seller's proceeds and paid through payroll at or immediately after Completion; or require the Seller to fund them pre-Completion with evidence. Insert a specific indemnity for any shortfall and for employer on-costs. Request the Seller's calculation of on-costs now.

### 2.11 Ironquay IP – Clause 11.1
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Scope | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Broaden, preserving the SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 not independently verified either way |

**Analysis.** Under DD-004 cl. 7.3, SOW3 Project Materials do not transfer until *every* SOW3 fee is paid in cleared funds. If AUD 180,000 is open, the Company does not own that IP today. An indemnity capped at the payment amount covers the cost of curing but not the consequential exposure if title cannot be perfected (e.g. Ironquay insolvency, dispute over amounts, or Ironquay licensing the materials elsewhere). We should not assume the AUD 180,000 is either owed or paid – DD-010 is an internal ledger.

**Position.** Pre-Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay (preserving the cl. 7.3 cure path). Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own or have unencumbered rights in the SOW3 Project Materials, including costs of re-procurement or re-development, third-party claims and any further amounts Ironquay asserts. Keep it outside Clause 12 limitations. Request bank evidence of payment status.

### 2.12 Export/privacy incident (DD-006) – Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Characterisation | "Preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way |

**Analysis.** The Disclosure Letter (para 6) is more candid than the Update: ~1,240 records of personal information (names, business emails, roles, timestamps) sent to an unintended external address; access, scope and notifiability unknown. We should neither accept "not material" nor assert that it is a notifiable breach – the facts do not yet support either. The risk is that the Seller's general disclosure (1.1) plus the knowledge bar (8.3) would convert this into a disclosed-and-known matter with no recourse, regardless of what the investigation finds.

**Position.** (a) Pre-Completion covenants: preserve all logs and evidence; complete the investigation with a report to Buyer; notify Buyer of any development; consult Buyer before any regulator or data-subject notification; (b) specific indemnity for loss arising from the DD-006 incident (regulatory, notification, remediation, third-party claims), outside Clause 12 and not qualified by disclosure or knowledge; (c) no price adjustment or demand at this stage; reserve position pending the report.

### 2.13 Sandbar supplier renewals (AUD 330,000)
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Characterisation | Ordinary-course operating costs | Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction |

**Analysis.** Three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each, to be read together (DD-008/DD-011). The Seller does not state whether they are committed, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course (Disclosure Letter para 8). They may well be ordinary-course, in which case our playbook does not treat them as Debt. The question is whether they were entered into or renewed in a way that pre-commits the Company post-Completion, or whether any amount has accrued pre-Completion and should sit in working capital/Debt.

**Position.** Do not deduct from price at this stage. Request: renewal dates, term, termination rights, and whether any amount is accrued or prepaid at the Locked Box / Completion Accounts date. Add a Warranty on supplier commitments and ensure the conduct-of-business covenants require consent for any further renewals above a threshold. Reassess once information received.

### 2.14 Tax / IP – "settled under the general regime"
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Status | Settled; subject to general cap/basket/time limits | OPEN; no unlimited liability assumed; no resolution assumed |

**Analysis.** Nothing has been agreed. Folding Tax and IP into the general regime would subject the Tax indemnity to the 18-month period (before most ATO review periods have even run) and the AUD 4.8m cap. We should not overclaim an unlimited Tax indemnity in our response either – the point is to reject the Seller's unilateral "settlement" and keep the categories separate for a standalone negotiation.

**Position.** Record that Tax and IP Warranties and the Tax indemnity remain open and will be the subject of separate regimes (separate caps and periods, Tax period aligned to statutory review periods plus a margin). Expressly exclude them from the Clause 12.3 "all Claims" default.

### 2.15 Title evidence – DD-012
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Evidence | Company share register at DD-012 | Independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a supplied internal source |

**Analysis.** The share register is maintained by the Company (controlled by the Seller) and is the Seller's own document. Disclosure Letter para 10 concedes it is merely "the source relied on" and that Buyer verification is not done. It does not evidence absence of encumbrances (Riverlark security may extend to the shares), options, pre-emptive rights or the Seller's authority.

**Position.** Pre-Completion/Completion deliverables: current ASIC company extract and member search; PPSR search against Company and Seller; share certificates or confirmation of uncertificated holding; Seller board/shareholder resolutions and constitution; confirmation of no options, convertible securities or shareholder agreements. Fundamental Warranties on title, capacity and authority under the separate 100% / 6-year regime. Buyer diligence team to complete its own ASIC/PPSR searches now, before responding.

### 2.16 Other disclosed matters (not in Seller Update)
- **Office lease (DD-007):** notification obligation only, per Seller. Confirm by reviewing DD-007 directly; if consent is in fact required, add as CP or Seller covenant. Add a pre-Completion covenant to give the notification.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** restriction on assignment; Seller says not triggered by a share sale. Verify whether DD-009 contains any change-of-control language distinct from assignment. If none, accept, but include within the Material Contracts warranty.

---

## 3. Structural concerns running across the draft

1. **Interlocking override.** Clauses 8.3 + 12.3 "all Claims" + 12.8/20.5 "any nature" + Disclosure 1.1/1.2 + Fundamental-into-general operate as a single system designed to leave the Buyer with virtually no Warranty recourse. Each must be unwound; conceding any one of them weakens the others.
2. **Disclosure Letter versus Seller Update.** On Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses and title, the Disclosure Letter admits the facts the Seller Update glosses over. Our response should cite the Disclosure Letter paragraphs directly.
3. **Authority.** Two Seller positions (20% cap, 18 months) land on our conditional fallbacks. No written authority from Amelia Frost exists for this draft. The team should not treat them as "close enough" to accept.
4. **No-admission reservation (1.4 / 11).** Harmless as a statement, but must not be allowed to operate as a limitation of liability.

---

## 4. Summary of recommendations

**Non-negotiable (no concession authority):**
1. Full fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance.
2. Separate Fundamental/Title regime: 100% cap, ≥ 6 years, outside de minimis/basket/knowledge bar.
3. Delete Clause 8.3 buyer-knowledge bar in its entirety.
4. Delete the Clause 12.3 "applies to all Claims" default; replace with an express scope clause confining Clause 12 to general Warranty Claims.

**Revert to playbook opening position (fallbacks unauthorised):**
5. Cap 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
6. De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; tipping (first-dollar) recovery.
7. 24-month general claims period.
8. Specific fair disclosure only; delete whole-data-room and public-register general disclosure.

**Completion mechanics:**
9. Bluefen: CP requiring unconditional consent plus evidence that cl. 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion; "reasonable endeavours" and "satisfied on delivery" rejected.
10. Riverlark: payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, security releases at Completion; post-Completion release rejected absent irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.
11. Bonuses: AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item deducted from Seller proceeds (or Seller-funded with evidence), plus shortfall indemnity.
12. Title: independent ASIC/PPSR searches, certificates, authority documents; DD-012 is not accepted as proof.

**Specific-risk items (information requests + indemnities, no price adjustment yet):**
13. Ironquay: evidence of cleared SOW3 payment and confirmatory assignment as deliverables; broaden indemnity beyond the payment amount, preserving cl. 7.3 cure.
14. DD-006: evidence-preservation and investigation covenants, Buyer consultation on notifications, specific indemnity; no characterisation of breach/harm either way.
15. Sandbar: request terms and accrual position; no automatic Debt treatment.
16. Lease and Mossvale: verify DD-007 and DD-009 source documents; add notification covenant.

**Open items to be flagged as not agreed:**
17. Tax and IP regimes – reject the Seller's "settled under the general regime"; record as open for separate negotiation without asserting unlimited liability.

**Internal action:** before the mark-up goes out, (i) confirm with Amelia Frost whether any fallback authority is to be given for this draft (recommend none at this stage, to preserve trading value), and (ii) have the diligence team run independent ASIC and PPSR searches on Paperbark Analytics and Harbourglass Ventures so the title response is evidence-based.
=== END ADVICE ===
